The implementation is complete and the full test suite is green (BUILD SUCCESS, 1 test passing — the other two files in the acceptance package are support base classes, not test classes).

## Summary

I implemented the customerCode de-duplication rule in `ClinicServiceImpl.java`:

- **`generateCustomerCode(Owner)`** now computes the base code (`<REGION>-<HASH8>`) as before, then passes it through a new de-duplication step.
- **`deduplicateCustomerCode(String base)`** collects all existing owners' `customerCode` values. If the base code is unused, it's returned unchanged; otherwise it appends `-<n>` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 that isn't already taken (checking both the bare base and prior `-<n>` de-duplications).

This runs before membership-number generation, so the derived `membershipNumber` correctly picks up the de-duplicated code. Added the `java.util.stream.Collectors` import. The `coreCustomerCodesStayUnique` acceptance test — which asserts distinct owners always get distinct customerCodes — passes.

I implemented the customerCode de-duplication rule in `ClinicServiceImpl.java`:

- **`generateCustomerCode(Owner)`** now computes the base code (`<REGION>-<HASH8>`) as before, then passes it through a new de-duplication step.
- **`deduplicateCustomerCode(String base)`** collects all existing owners' `customerCode` values. If the base code is unused, it's returned unchanged; otherwise it appends `-<n>` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 that isn't already taken (checking both the bare base and prior `-<n>` de-duplications).

This runs before membership-number generation, so the derived `membershipNumber` correctly picks up the de-duplicated code. Added the `java.util.stream.Collectors` import. The `coreCustomerCodesStayUnique` acceptance test — which asserts distinct owners always get distinct customerCodes — passes.
